_comment: Earth viewer config for make-planet-viewer.py. All values here differ from the Mars source template.

core_layer_data.name: Crust
core_layer_data.description: Earth's outermost layer, divided into thin dense oceanic crust (~7 km) and thicker buoyant continental crust (~35–70 km). Both types form tectonic plates that move, collide, and subduct, driving earthquakes, mountain building, and volcanic activity at plate boundaries.
core_layer_data.composition: Oceanic: basalt and gabbro (mafic). Continental: granite-dominated silicates (felsic), with metamorphic and sedimentary cover.

core_layer_data.name: Mantle
core_layer_data.description: Earth's largest layer, comprising ~84% of the planet's volume. Slow thermal convection drives plate tectonics, transports heat from the core, and enables volcanism at subduction zones, hotspots, and mid-ocean ridges. Divided into an upper mantle, a transition zone (410–660 km), and a lower mantle (perovskite-dominated).
core_layer_data.composition: Peridotite (olivine, pyroxene, garnet) grading to high-pressure silicate phases. The lower mantle is dominated by bridgmanite (Mg-perovskite) and ferropericlase.

core_layer_data.name: Outer Core
core_layer_data.description: A shell of liquid iron-nickel alloy from 2,890 to 5,150 km depth. Convective flow of this electrically conductive fluid generates Earth's global magnetic field through a self-sustaining geodynamo, shielding the surface from harmful cosmic radiation and solar wind.
core_layer_data.composition: Liquid iron-nickel alloy with ~10% lighter elements (oxygen, sulfur, silicon). Electrical conductivity drives the geomagnetic field.

core_layer_data.name: Inner Core
core_layer_data.description: A dense solid sphere at Earth's centre, from 5,150 km depth to the planet's centre (~1,220 km radius). Despite temperatures near 5,000°C, it remains solid due to immense pressure exceeding 330 GPa. It grows slowly as the outer core cools and solidifies.
core_layer_data.depth: 5,150 km depth to centre (~1,220 km radius)
core_layer_data.composition: Solid iron-nickel alloy with traces of lighter elements. Seismically anisotropic, with faster wave speeds along the rotation axis.

temperature.label: Mean Surface Temperature
temperature.description: Estimated mean surface temperature derived from latitude and terrain elevation using the standard atmosphere lapse rate (6.5 °C/km).

pressure.label: Atmospheric Pressure
pressure.description: Estimated surface atmospheric pressure using the barometric formula. Highest at sea level and ocean trenches (~101,325 Pa), lowest at high mountain summits.

wind.label: Surface Wind Speed
wind.description: Estimated mean surface wind speed. Strongest near mid-latitude jet streams (40–60°) and at high elevation.

irradiance.label: Solar Irradiance
irradiance.description: Estimated mean annual solar irradiance at the surface, accounting for ~60% average cloud cover. Peak near the equator (~600 W/m²), minimal at poles.

radiation.label: UV Index
radiation.description: Estimated UV index at the surface. Highest near the equator and at high-altitude sites where the solar angle is favourable and atmospheric UV absorption is reduced.

diurnal.label: Diurnal Temp Range
diurnal.description: Estimated daily temperature swing between day and night. Largest in continental interior deserts, smallest in maritime and equatorial zones.

atm_density.label: Atmospheric Density
atm_density.description: Atmospheric density ρ = P / (R·T). Densest at sea level (~1.225 kg/m³), thinnest at high mountain summits (~0.5 kg/m³).

sound_speed.label: Speed of Sound
sound_speed.description: Speed of sound c = √(γRT) in air (γ = 1.4). Decreases with altitude as temperature drops with the standard lapse rate.

co2_frost.label: Sea Ice Probability
co2_frost.description: Probability of sea ice formation based on latitude-derived mean temperature. Ice forms where mean temperature drops below −2°C; confined to polar and sub-polar regions.

slope.label: Slope Gradient
slope.description: Terrain slope magnitude derived from the GEBCO elevation model. Steepest at continental shelf edges, mountain ranges, and ocean trench walls.

roughness.label: Terrain Roughness
roughness.description: Local elevation standard deviation over ~90 km windows. Smooth abyssal plains are blue; heavily faulted mountain belts and rugged coasts are red.

ice_depth.label: Permafrost Thickness
ice_depth.description: Estimated permafrost thickness using a geothermal gradient of 45 mK/m. Deepest under Siberia and the Canadian Arctic, zero in temperate and tropical latitudes.

dust_devil.label: Convective Instability
dust_devil.description: Surface convective instability index proportional to estimated diurnal heating relative to pressure. Highest in continental tropical and high-altitude regions.

landing_score.label: Habitability Score
landing_score.description: Composite surface habitability index combining temperature, pressure, UV exposure, terrain flatness, and water potential.

solar_output.label: Solar Panel Output
solar_output.description: Estimated electrical output for a horizontal solar panel (22% efficiency), accounting for typical cloud cover. Best at equatorial and high-altitude sites.

brine_stability.label: Surface Water Potential
brine_stability.description: Fraction of surface conditions where liquid water is thermodynamically stable based on temperature and elevation. Highest in tropical lowland regions.

magnetic_shielding.label: Magnetic Shielding
magnetic_shielding.description: Earth's global magnetic field provides strong radiation shielding at mid-latitudes. Reduced near the geomagnetic poles and in the South Atlantic Anomaly.

habitability.label: Human Habitability Score
habitability.description: Composite human habitability index combining temperature, pressure, UV exposure, water potential, terrain, and solar energy availability.

tour_mode_facets.label: Landforms
tour_mode_facets.description: Major mountains, basins, deserts, ice sheets, and ocean-basin reference features.

tour_mode_facets.label: Ocean basins
tour_mode_facets.description: Ocean basins and bathymetric reference points.

tour_mode_facets.label: Volcanic and tectonic
tour_mode_facets.description: Volcanoes, spreading ridges, rift zones, and plate-boundary features.

tour_mode_facets.label: Launch sites
tour_mode_facets.description: Major Earth launch sites connected to spaceflight history and operations.

tour_mode_facets.label: Storm belts
tour_mode_facets.description: Representative atmospheric corridors, storm belts, and convergence zones.

tour_mode_facets.label: Moon system
tour_mode_facets.description: Earth's Moon and selected lunar surface references.

moon_data.name: Moon
moon_data.description: Earth's only natural satellite, a geochemically differentiated body with a solid iron inner core, a partially molten outer core, a thick silicate mantle, and a highland anorthosite and mare basalt crust. Formed ~4.5 Ga from debris ejected by a giant impact between Earth and a Mars-sized protoplanet called Theia.

moon_feature_data.name: Tycho Crater
moon_feature_data.description: Young, geologically recent (109 Ma) impact crater with an extensive bright ray system spanning nearly half the lunar surface. The rays are among the most prominent telescopic features of the Moon.

moon_feature_data.name: Mare Imbrium
moon_feature_data.description: Largest lava-flooded circular basin on the lunar near side. Formed ~3.9 Ga by a giant impact, subsequently flooded by basaltic lava between 3.5 and 3.0 Ga.

moon_feature_data.name: Oceanus Procellarum
moon_feature_data.description: Largest mare on the Moon, covering most of the western near side. Unlike most circular maria, it lacks a clear impact basin rim, suggesting it may overlie a region of concentrated heat-producing elements called the Procellarum KREEP Terrane.

moon_feature_data.name: South Pole-Aitken Basin
moon_feature_data.description: One of the largest and oldest impact basins in the Solar System, on the lunar far side. With a diameter of ~2,500 km and depth of ~8 km, it exposes the deepest crustal material accessible for future sample return.

moon_feature_data.name: Copernicus Crater
moon_feature_data.description: A prominent 93 km impact crater with well-preserved terraced walls, a central peak complex, and a young bright ray system.

moon_feature_data.name: Shackleton Crater
moon_feature_data.description: Permanently shadowed crater at the lunar south pole with confirmed water ice. A primary candidate for a future lunar base due to nearby solar-illuminated peaks and ice resources.

moon_feature_data.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
moon_feature_data.description: Apollo 11 landing site. A smooth basalt plain where astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin first walked on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

moon_feature_data.name: Aristarchus Crater
moon_feature_data.description: The brightest large crater on the Moon and an active spectral anomaly site. Surrounded by pyroclastic deposits from the nearby Aristarchus Plateau volcanic complex.

label_data.name: Mount Everest
label_data.description: Highest point above sea level on Earth, located in the central Himalaya. Built by the ongoing India-Eurasia collision, the summit sits in the jet stream and experiences some of the most extreme weather on the planet.

label_data.name: K2
label_data.description: Second highest peak on Earth, on the China-Pakistan border in the Karakoram range. Notorious for its technical difficulty and high fatality rate among climbers.

label_data.name: Mariana Trench
label_data.description: Deepest known point on Earth, the Challenger Deep reaches approximately 10,930 m below sea level. Formed by Pacific oceanic crust subducting beneath the Mariana plate.

label_data.name: Pacific Ocean
label_data.description: Largest ocean basin on Earth, covering more area than all land combined. Bounded by subduction zones around its rim and spreading centres across its floor.

label_data.name: Atlantic Ocean
label_data.description: Ocean basin defined by the Mid-Atlantic Ridge at its centre and passive continental margins on either side. Formed by the breakup of Pangaea around 200 Ma.

label_data.name: Indian Ocean
label_data.description: Third largest ocean basin, bordered by Africa, Asia, and Australia. The northern basin is landlocked and receives monsoon-driven freshwater inputs.

label_data.name: Arctic Ocean
label_data.description: Smallest and shallowest of Earth's ocean basins, mostly covered by sea ice. The Arctic is warming at roughly four times the global average rate.

label_data.name: Southern Ocean
label_data.description: Circumpolar ocean surrounding Antarctica. Defined by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, it connects all other ocean basins and drives deep global thermohaline circulation.

label_data.name: Himalaya
label_data.description: Major continental collision belt formed by the ongoing convergence of the Indian and Eurasian plates. Home to all fourteen 8,000-metre peaks on Earth.

label_data.name: Andes
label_data.description: Long volcanic and tectonic arc along western South America, formed by subduction of the Nazca plate. The longest continental mountain range on Earth.

label_data.name: Alps
label_data.description: European mountain belt formed by collision of the African and Eurasian plates. Glaciated during the Pleistocene, the Alps radiate major river systems northward and southward.

label_data.name: Rocky Mountains
label_data.description: Broad cordilleran belt along western North America formed by multiple accretionary episodes. The Continental Divide separates Pacific and Atlantic drainage.

label_data.name: Amazon Basin
label_data.description: Largest river basin and tropical rainforest on Earth. The Amazon River discharges roughly 20% of global freshwater river runoff into the Atlantic.

label_data.name: Congo Basin
label_data.description: Second largest tropical rainforest basin, centred on the Congo River drainage in central Africa.

label_data.name: Sahara
label_data.description: Largest hot desert on Earth, spanning most of North Africa. The Sahara oscillates between dry and wet phases driven by orbital forcing over 100,000-year cycles.

label_data.name: Antarctic Ice Sheet
label_data.description: Largest ice sheet on Earth, storing approximately 26.5 million km³ of ice. Full melting would raise sea level by roughly 58 metres.

label_data.name: Greenland Ice Sheet
label_data.description: Second largest ice sheet on Earth, covering most of Greenland. Rapid melt is contributing significantly to current sea-level rise.

label_data.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
label_data.description: Divergent plate boundary and volcanic ridge running the full length of the Atlantic Ocean. Separates the North and South American plates from the Eurasian and African plates.

label_data.name: East Pacific Rise
label_data.description: Fast-spreading mid-ocean ridge in the eastern Pacific, diverging at up to 150 mm/yr. A major source of oceanic crust and hydrothermal vent activity.

label_data.name: Great Rift Valley
label_data.description: Active continental rift system extending from the Afar Triple Junction south through Tanzania. The East African Rift is actively splitting Africa apart.

label_data.name: Mauna Loa
label_data.description: One of Earth's largest active shield volcanoes, built above the Hawaiian hotspot. Together with neighbouring Mauna Kea, forms the largest volcanic mountain on Earth by volume.

label_data.name: Mauna Kea
label_data.description: Tallest mountain on Earth measured from its oceanic base. Home to major astronomical observatories exploiting its exceptional atmospheric clarity.

label_data.name: Mount Etna
label_data.description: Most active volcano in Europe and one of the most continuously erupting volcanoes in the world.

label_data.name: Mount Fuji
label_data.description: Iconic stratovolcano and highest peak in Japan. Last erupted in 1707 and considered an active volcano with ongoing geothermal activity.

label_data.name: Kilauea
label_data.description: One of the world's most active volcanoes on the flanks of Mauna Loa in Hawaii. Continuously erupting with effusive lava flows since 1983.

label_data.name: Yellowstone Caldera
label_data.description: Active supervolcanic system above the Yellowstone hotspot. The last major eruption 640,000 years ago ejected roughly 1,000 km³ of material.

label_data.name: Iceland
label_data.description: Island built on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and above the Iceland hotspot. One of the most volcanically productive regions on Earth per unit area.

label_data.name: Grand Canyon
label_data.description: Iconic erosional gorge carved by the Colorado River through nearly 2 billion years of sedimentary and crystalline rock.

label_data.name: Challenger Deep
label_data.description: The deepest known point on Earth, located in the southern Mariana Trench. Reaches approximately 10,935 m below sea level.

label_data.name: Tonga Trench
label_data.description: Among the deepest oceanic trenches on Earth, site of the fastest-subducting plate boundary.

label_data.name: North Atlantic Hurricane Belt
label_data.description: Primary track for Atlantic tropical cyclones and hurricanes. Storms develop over warm tropical Atlantic water and track northwestward before curving northeast.

label_data.name: Intertropical Convergence Zone
label_data.description: Persistent low-latitude belt of ascending air, deep convection, and heavy rainfall. Migrates north and south with the seasons, driving monsoonal precipitation.

label_data.name: Southern Ocean Storm Track
label_data.description: Circumpolar belt of intense westerly winds and frequent extratropical cyclone development. The most consistently stormy region on Earth.

label_data.name: Bay of Bengal Cyclone Track
label_data.description: High-frequency cyclone development zone over the Bay of Bengal, affecting densely populated coastal areas of South Asia each monsoon season.

label_data.name: Kennedy Space Center
label_data.description: Primary NASA launch facility on the Atlantic coast of Florida. Home to Apollo, Space Shuttle, and current Commercial Crew launches.

label_data.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
label_data.description: Oldest and largest operational space launch facility in the world, in Kazakhstan. Used for Sputnik, Vostok, Soyuz, and Proton launches.

label_data.name: Guiana Space Centre
label_data.description: European Space Agency primary launch site near Kourou in French Guiana. Near-equatorial location provides significant launch performance advantage.

label_data.name: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre
label_data.description: China's oldest space launch facility in the Gobi Desert, used for crewed Shenzhou missions and key satellite launches.

label_data.name: Satish Dhawan Space Centre
label_data.description: India's primary launch site on Sriharikota Island in the Bay of Bengal. Home of ISRO's PSLV and GSLV launchers.
